model_annotation: The figure presents two line plots comparing the training reward performance of two reinforcement learning methods—“Llama-On-Policy” and “Llama-LUFFY”—on “Easy” and “Hard” training sets, respectively. In the top plot (“Easy Training Set”), the x-axis represents training steps ranging from 0 to approximately 500 on a linear scale, while the y-axis shows training rewards from 0.0 to 0.4, also linear. The blue line with circular markers (“Llama-On-Policy-Easy”) and the red line with square markers (“Llama-LUFFY-Easy”) both start near 0.0, rise steeply in the first 100 steps, and then plateau near 0.4 with minor fluctuations; the red line shows slightly higher variance but similar final performance. In the bottom plot (“Hard Training Set”), the x-axis again spans 0 to 500 steps, while the y-axis ranges from 0.0 to 0.2. Here, the blue line (“Llama-On-Policy-Hard”) begins near 0.0 and drops to nearly 0.0 after 100 steps, remaining flat thereafter. In contrast, the red line (“Llama-LUFFY-Hard”) rises gradually from 0.0 to approximately 0.2 by step 500, with visible noise and a slight upward trend. A faint gray annotation labeled “1” appears near the upper right of the bottom plot, likely indicating a reference point or footnote. Both plots include shaded regions around each line, representing uncertainty or standard deviation across runs.
